meta.title: Lawn mowing in Ortonville, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Weekly lawn service in Ortonville and Brandon Township: big rural lots and village yards mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off, finished in clean stripes.

hero.title: Acreage trimmed **to the far fence.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows Ortonville and Brandon Township lawns every week, from village yards near the mill to acreage along the back roads: mowed, trimmed, edged along the drive and blown off, with stripes that run the length of the lot.

local.title: Many Brandon Township lots run **one to five acres.**
local.intro: Much of the township is one to five acre parcels on rolling ground. That changes the mowing: wider decks, longer runs and more trim work along fences, ditches and tree lines.

points.title: Acreage is normal here
points.body: One of our customers has us on a 7 1/2 acre lawn all year and says so in a review. Mowing acreage well is about keeping the lines straight across a long run, and keeping the trim work just as tidy at the far end of the property as by the front door.

points.title: Sandy rises, wet swales
points.body: The ground around the village is sandy, and much of the township's low ground is muck. In a dry spell the rises brown first, and in a wet spring the swales stay soft. Mowing at about 3 inches and taking no more than a third, as MSU Extension advises, helps the dry spots most.

points.title: Ditches and the creek
points.body: Roadside ditches in Brandon Township drain to Kearsley Creek, a cold water trout stream that suffers from sediment washing in. We blow clippings back onto the grass, never down the slope into the ditch.

points.title: Village yards
points.body: In the village, lots sit closer together and the walks and curbs show every edge. Those get a sharp edging line and a blown off walk, the same care the big lots get along a long drive.

logistics.title: How we price and mow an Ortonville lot.
body: You get a set mowing day, so the gate, the dogs and the kids' toys can be planned around it. Each visit is the full job: mowing, trimming around trees, beds and fence lines, edging along the drive and walks, and a final blow off.

Rob prices a big lot after he has walked it, because on acreage the time is in the trimming as much as the open lawn. For the start and end of the season, see [leaf removal in Ortonville](/leaf-removal-ortonville-mi/) and our [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup/) service.

faq.q: Is there a lawn service in Ortonville, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes provides weekly lawn service in Ortonville and Brandon Township: mowing, trimming, edging and a blown off finish, on a set day each week. Call or [text Rob](sms:+18109903040) for a free estimate.

faq.q: Do you mow large rural lots?
faq.a: Yes. Acreage is normal around Ortonville, and one of our reviewers has us on a 7 1/2 acre lawn all year. The price covers both the open lawn and the trim work, so it is set after the estimate visit.

faq.q: What height should my lawn be cut in summer?
faq.a: Around 3 inches or a little more, per MSU Extension, and never more than a third of the blade at a time. On sandy Brandon Township ground that dries out fast, the taller cut shades the soil and holds up better through a dry August.

faq.q: Do you mow down to the road ditch?
faq.a: Yes, the part of the lawn you keep mowed now, including the slope toward the ditch where a mower can run safely. Clippings stay on the grass instead of going into the ditch, since ditches here feed creeks like Kearsley Creek.
